why: A mixed project: .tsx (JSX + types) -> .jsx -> .ts -> .js. Each file must be parsed in ITS OWN mode, otherwise JSX or types break the parse and the imports vanish. Zero parse errors is the key assertion. The graph normalizes each module to plain JS (strip types + lower JSX) BEFORE extracting its dependencies — and the JSX transform INJECTS `import { jsx } from 'react/jsx-runtime'`. Seeing it here is the CORRECT behaviour: a bundler ignoring it would emit code referencing `jsx` without ever importing it.
